question: The amount on a sum of ₹3,500 at 20% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective compound interest rate for 2 years at 20% = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = 44%

Total amount after 2 years = 100% (Principal) + 44% (Interest) = 144%

Amount = 144% of 3500 = 1.44 × 3500 = 5040

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,040.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹3,500

Rate (R) = 20% per annum

Time (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
 
• 
 + 20% 
 + 20% Start (Year 0) ₹3,500 Year 1 ₹4,200 Year 2 A = ? 

**Calculation:**

⇒ A = 3500 × (1 + 20/100)²

⇒ A = 3500 × (1 + 1/5)²

⇒ A = 3500 × (6/5) × (6/5)

⇒ A = 3500 × 36 ÷ 25

⇒ A = 140 × 36

⇒ A = 5040

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,040.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Compound Interest

For 2 years, the effective compound interest rate can be found using the successive percentage formula: Rₑff = 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%.

Difference Between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest on a certain sum for exactly 2 years is calculated directly as: D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual rate becomes half (R ÷ 2) and the time periods are doubled (2n).
